messages.subject: X2 statistics in mirt
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying t analyze my data using UIRT model and MIRT model in mirt.
I wrote this;

#
resultA_re1<-mirt(TIMSS2011jpn_re1,1,method="MHRM",itemtype="2PL");resultA_re1 #探索的因子分析
summary(resultA_re1)
coef(resultA_re1)

#
modelC_re1<-mirt.model() 
F1=1,9,11,12,13,16,18,27,30,31,32,33,39,44,47,49,51,59,62,63,64,69,70,72,74,77,80,81,83,85,86,87,90,91,92,93,96,101,104,105,107,110,111,112,118,119,120,121,124,126,127,129,130,131,135,136,139,150,151,152,153,157,164,166,168,170,172,173,178,179,183,184,185,186,190,199,203,205
F2=2,3,4,5,6,7,8,20,21,23,24,25,26,29,35,40,46,53,54,56,60,65,68,76,78,79,98,100,123,125,133,137,138,140,143,144,147,158,159,160,162,163,177,181,189,195,197,198,202,206,207,209
F3=10,14,15,17,19,22,28,34,36,37,38,41,42,43,45,48,50,52,55,57,58,61,66,67,71,73,75,82,84,88,89,94,95,97,99,102,103,106,108,109,113,114,115,116,117,122,128,132,134,141,142,145,146,148,149,154,155,156,161,165,167,169,171,174,175,176,180,182,187,188,191,192,193,194,196,200,201,204,208,210,211,212,213,214
COV=F1*F2*F3
resultC_re1<-mirt(TIMSS2011jpn_re1,modelC_re1,itemtype="2PL",method="MHRM",technical = list(NCYCLES = 100000));resultC_re1
summary(resultC_re1)
coef(resultC_re1)

So,
> anova(resultA_re1,resultC_re1)

Model 1: mirt(data = TIMSS2011jpn_re1, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL", method = "MHRM")
Model 2: mirt(data = TIMSS2011jpn_re1, model = modelC_re1, itemtype = "2PL", 
    method = "MHRM", technical = list(NCYCLES = 1e+05))

       AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC    logLik     X2  df   p
1 130512.3 130604.6 131887.7 133247.7 -64828.16    NaN NaN NaN
2 130545.0 130638.7 131930.1 133299.6 -64841.52 -26.73   3   1

I don't understand that X2 is minus in anova.

model1 is UIRT model.
model2 is MIRT model  (factors=3, COV=F1*F2*F3).

Please give me advice,

thanks

Yutaro.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: X2 statistics in mirt
parts:
This can happen with the MHRM algorithm because it is stochastic, so parameters are only approximations of the true ML estimates. However, note that these models are not nested, so you can't really use a X2 test anyway. Use the information criteria like AIC and BIC to inform your modeling decision (in this case the UIRT model fits about as well as the MIRT, so nothing is really gained). You could also compare goodness of fit with M2() to see if there is any modeling improvements, but I doubt it given how close these models match the data.

Phil
